en: The Mahāyāna Tri-saṃvara-pāpadeśanā Sūtra,
translated at Daxingshan Monastery during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by Jñānagupta, Gupta, and others.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Bhagavān was staying in the Great Radiant Forest at Vaiśālī, together with a great assembly of more than a thousand bhikṣus, as well as immeasurable bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded by an immeasurable multitude of hundreds of thousands of beings, who stood before and behind him as he preached the Dharma.

At that moment, the Elder Śāriputra was seated in that assembly; receiving the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, he rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Buddha, spoke these words:
“I now wish to ask a question; I pray that the Buddha will grant me permission to explain it for my sake.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: "You, Śāriputra!
Ask whatever you wish; I shall explain it so as to gladden your heart."

At that time, the Elder Śāriputra, having received the Buddha’s permission to explain what he had been asked, was filled with such joy and exultation that he could not contain himself; with a heart full of joy, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Virtuous World-Honored One!..."
If good sons and good daughters and others wish to abide in the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas,
or abide in the Mahāyāna, how should these sentient beings, who possess various karmic obstructions, perform repentance?
What is disclosure?
It refers to the obscuration of afflictions, the obscuration of sentient beings, the obscuration of dharmas, and the obscuration regarding future lives.
What is repentance? What is disclosure?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, you, Śāriputra!"
You now desire to bring great peace, happiness, and benefit to gods and humans by being able to question the Tathāgata on such a matter.
You, Śāriputra! You should now listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well; I shall speak for your sake.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Excellent, World-Honored One!
We only pray that you will explain this.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

If good sons or good daughters—whether those who have resolved to abide in the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, or those who abide in the Mahāyāna—these sentient beings should, during each of the three periods of the day and night, rise from their seats, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees on the ground, join their palms with ten fingers together, and speak these words:”

"All the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions—whether staying in the world, sitting, or walking—may these World-Honored Ones remember me, may they bear witness to me; may they act as my eyes, may they act as my wisdom, may they act as my excellence, and may they act as my ultimate refuge. Before them, I repent and reveal my transgressions."

Whatever karmic obstructions I have accumulated throughout beginningless saṃsāra as I wandered and transmigrated—whether in this life or in other lives; whether committed by myself, caused to be committed by others, or rejoiced in seeing others commit them—including obstructions of afflictions (*kleśa-āvaraṇa*), obstructions regarding sentient beings, obstructions regarding the Dharma, and obstructions that hinder future rebirths; whether initially committed by myself, caused to be committed by others, or rejoiced in seeing others commit them for the first time; whether currently being committed by myself, caused to be committed by others, or rejoiced in seeing others committing them; or whether already completed by myself, caused to be completed by others, or rejoiced in seeing others having completed them.

Furthermore, when one has not yet recognized the Buddha, has not yet recognized the Dharma, and has not yet recognized the Saṅgha; when one does not yet know what is wholesome and does not yet know what is unwholesome; when one gives rise to various evils by following after desire, hatred, delusion, greed, and a distracted mind; or when one is overwhelmed by sleep; or when one is restless and playful; or when one harbors doubt; or when one is deceitful and crooked; or when one lacks shame and a sense of moral dread.

Furthermore, if one is conceited, arrogant, and haughty; or gives rise to resentment and malice; or becomes intoxicated by negligence; or, with an evil mind, sheds the blood of a Buddha, slanders the True Dharma, causes a schism in the Saṃgha, kills an Arhat, or kills one's father or mother.

Regarding such karmas as these: whether one performs them oneself—having begun, being in the process of performing, or having already completed them—or causes others to perform them, or sees them being performed and rejoices therein;

whether through the three types of bodily karma, the four types of vocal karma, or the three types of mental karma; whether one gives rise to various evil intentions toward sentient beings; or whether one oppresses, harms, insults, or reviles those of the Three Vehicles, speaking of their faults, harboring resentment, or slandering them; or whether one engages in sexual misconduct or holds wrong views.
Whether at the initial commencement, while in the process of performing, or after having completed it—whether acting for oneself, instructing others, or rejoicing in the act;

or if, contrary to what has been taught, one violates the collection of precepts, steals property belonging to a stūpa, or gives rise to wrong views—whether at the first resolution, during the performance, or upon its completion.
Such evils as these—one commits oneself, incites others to commit, or rejoices upon seeing them committed.

Or one acts in opposition toward one’s parents; or obstructs others from leaving the household life; or when another is about to receive full ordination, creates obstacles by withholding their robes; or creates hindrances at the time of entering meditative concentration or during right mindfulness; or creates obstacles regarding gain, fame, and roots of goodness. Regarding such matters, whether they are first initiated, while being performed, or already completed, one does so oneself, incites others to do so, or rejoices upon seeing them done.
All such evil deeds as I have committed, I now confess and repent before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
May they bear witness for me; may they be my eyes, may they be my wisdom, may they be my excellence, and may they be my ultimate refuge.
Now, before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, I confess and reveal with a sincere heart, not daring to conceal anything; in future lives, I shall never dare to commit such acts again.
May all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, now take notice of me, accept me, and bear witness to this.

Whatever evil karma I have committed throughout the beginningless cycle of birth and death within the various afflictions—whether performed by myself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing it performed—all such karma that ought to result in an evil retribution, whether to be experienced in the present or in the future.
May all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, bear witness to me as if standing before my very eyes regarding these various karmas; may they grant me victory and grant me the ultimate.
Before all the Buddhas, I repent with a sincere heart and dare not conceal anything; in future lives, I shall never again commit such deeds.

All those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who existed in the past—just as they, when practicing the bodhisattva path in bygone times, confessed their karmic obstructions, afflictive obstructions, obstructions of sentient beings, dharma obstructions, and obstructions regarding future lives—and confessed in such a manner, I now likewise confess in this same way, not daring to conceal anything, and vowing never to commit them again in the future.

All the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the future world, just as they themselves practiced the bodhisattva path when they were cultivating it—confessing their karmic obstructions, afflictive obstructions, obstructions of sentient beings, obstructions to the Dharma, and obstructions regarding future lives, confessing them again and again after having already confessed them.
I now likewise repent of all such hindrances, confessing them openly and not daring to conceal them; having repented, I shall never dare to commit them again.

In all the worlds throughout the ten directions of the present, wherever there are Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently dwelling in the world—just as they, when practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, repented of karmic hindrances, afflictive hindrances, hindrances regarding sentient beings, hindrances regarding the Dharma, and hindrances that would lead to future lives, and having repented, repented yet again.

I now do likewise: I repent of karmic obstructions, afflictive obstructions, obstructions concerning all sentient beings, and obstructions that will arise in future lives; I repent and disclose them, not daring to conceal them, and vow never to commit them again in the future.

Thus, regarding all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present—whether they have already known, or will know—that I am now obscured by karmic obstructions and should fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts, or into the world of King Yama, or into places far removed from and contrary to the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, falling instead into places of oppression and suffering.

I now confess and repent of all such hindrances before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; may the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, bear witness to me as one who is most excellent and most supreme.
Before them, I have confessed and repented with a sincere heart, not daring to conceal anything, and I vow never to commit such acts again in future lives.

Now, I confess here with a sincere heart; may I and all sentient beings together purify all karmic obstructions regarding the dharmas, and may we purify all factors conducive to enlightenment so that they are fully fulfilled.
Thus he made this vow three times.

Just as the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past did, those Blessed Ones performed such repentance in former times; having repented in this way, they attained the unobstructed purity of all dharmas.

If there are Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in future ages, those World-Honored Ones shall likewise, having repented all karmic obstructions regarding all Buddhas in every world throughout the ten directions of the present, attain the unobstructed purity of all dharmas.

The Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently dwells in the world; when that Buddha, the World-Honored One, practiced in the past, he likewise repented his karmic obstructions in this manner and attained the unobstructed purity of all dharmas.

Śāriputra! For this reason, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to set out upon and abide in the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or abides in the Mahāyāna, and desires to purify their karmic obstructions, they should repent and disclose them in this manner, without concealing them, and resolve not to commit them again in future lives.

“Śāriputra! If there are good men or good women who wish to leave behind rebirth in the hells, as animals, as hungry ghosts, or in states of poverty and lowliness, they should likewise repent and disclose their transgressions without concealment, and resolve never to commit them again in future lives.”

Śāriputra! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to be born into a great clan of kṣatriyas, a great clan of brāhmaṇas, or a great household of householders to receive the fruits of merit and happiness; or if they further wish to be born in the abode of the Four Great Kings;
The Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven,
the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmapārṣadya Heaven,
the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, and the Bṛhatphala Heaven.
The gods of Limited Body, the gods of Immeasurable Body, the gods of Vast Fruit, the gods of Non-perception,
the gods of Light-Sound, the gods of No-Affliction, the gods of Good Vision, the Akaniṣṭha gods, the gods of the Sphere of Infinite Space,
the gods of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, the gods of the Sphere of Nothingness, and the gods of the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-Perception.

If you wish to be born there and experience that same retribution together with them, you should repent of your karmic obstructions in this manner; you should thus disclose them without concealment, and resolve never to commit them again.
Therefore, Śāriputra!

Those who wish to attain the fruit of a srotāpanna, the fruit of a sakṛdāgāmin, the fruit of an anāgāmin, the fruit of an arhat, or the path of a pratyekabuddha, should likewise repent and disclose their transgressions to purify their karmic obstructions, and henceforth not commit them again.

Śāriputra! If there are good men or good women who wish to achieve the omniscience of unsurpassed bodhi, the incomparable wisdom, and the most supreme and wondrous wisdom of all the three realms, they should likewise repent and disclose their transgressions, vowing never to commit them again.

One should understand it thus: all dharmas spoken of by the Tathāgata arise from causes and conditions, and some possess arising and ceasing. Those of the past have already ceased; those of the future have not yet arrived; and those of the present lack substantiality. There is no karmic obstruction, nor is there any locus for karmic obstruction; even the various formations currently being performed are likewise without karmic obstruction.

Why is this so? The Tathāgata has constantly taught that all dharmas are empty and devoid of "mine"; there is no sentient being, no life-principle, no pudgala, no person, and no mānava; their intrinsic nature is empty and quiescent.
For this reason, all dharmas are free from karmic obstructions. Śāriputra,

if good men and good women are able to enter such limits— namely, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the limit of non-self, the limit of homelessness, and the limit of the outflow-free (*anāsrava*)— they will then be able to purify all dharma-obstructions and attain tranquility.
Thereupon, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How should these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Great Vehicle and have resolved their minds on Bodhicitta accord with and rejoice in the roots of goodness of all sentient beings?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“These sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should rise from their seats during the three periods of the day and the three periods of the night; they should bare their right shoulders, place their right knees upon the ground, join their palms together, and speak these words:

‘Whatever mass of merit belongs to all sentient beings included within the realm of sentient beings in all worlds—whether it was first performed, is being performed, or has already been performed; whether it was done by oneself, caused to be done by another, or rejoiced in while seeing it done; whether it was directed toward the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, or an individual (pudgala); whether it was the meritorious act of giving, the meritorious act of ethical discipline, or the meritorious act of meditative cultivation.’”

We now rejoice in all of that with the most excellent rejoicing—the greatest, the most wondrous, the most ultimate, the most pure, the peerless, the equal to the unequaled, the unsurpassed, and the supreme of the unsurpassed—authorized by all Buddhas; we should now rejoice in this manner.

All the accumulations of merit belonging to all the past Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Samyaksaṃbuddhas—from their first generation of the mind of awakening until their entry into nirvana without remainder—all such accumulations I now rejoice in with complete accord.

In all the worlds throughout the ten directions of the future, whatever Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas there shall be, and whatever accumulation of merit from the practice of the six pāramitās they may have undertaken from their first resolution—may I now rejoice in all of those in this very way, even as one rejoices with the approval of the Buddhas.

Furthermore, regarding all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently existing in all worlds throughout the ten directions—from their first generation of the mind of awakening until they have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and even until their entry into Nirvana without remainder—I now rejoice in all the accumulations of merit therein; I rejoice most excellently, and I rejoice even as the Buddhas permit such rejoicing.
“Śāriputra! What do you think? How much merit and great benefit are obtained from such a mass of merit resulting from sympathetic joy and harmony?”
Śāriputra! If all sentient beings contained within this trichiliocosm were to become arhats, [and if they were to give rise to the thought of awakening for the sake of others...]

If there are sons or daughters of good family who provide for, revere, and serve them, offering clothing, food and drink, medicinal decoctions, bedding, and other necessities until the end of their lives.
"Would the merit he thereby obtains not be great?
Śāriputra replied, "It would be very much."
"World-Honored One!
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!
Setting aside for a moment all the sentient beings included among the inhabitants of the trichiliocosm;

suppose, moreover, that all the sentient beings included among the inhabitants of as many worlds in the eastern direction as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River were all to attain the state of an Arhat.
If there are good sons or good daughters who, for as long as they live, provide offerings and provisions, even including medicinal decoctions—
Śāriputra, regarding all such matters:
"What do you think?
Is the merit obtained by that person not great? Śāriputra replied:
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"In this way, all sentient beings—those comprised within the category of sentient beings—in as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River throughout the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below, would all become arhats."
If there were good sons or good daughters who, for as long as they lived, made offerings, served, and provided for [this person], even with such things as clothing and medicinal decoctions—
would the merit they obtain not be great?
Śāriputra said: “Very many,
World-Honored One!”
"It is inconceivable that one can reach its limit.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"If sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna and have resolved their minds on awakening, being able to possess right faith free from all flattery and crookedness, resolve their minds on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and furthermore, are able to rejoice in this rejoicing in such a manner."

Śāriputra! That former merit does not equal even one hundredth part of this mass of merit; it does not equal one thousandth, one hundred-thousandth, one hundred-millionth, one ten-billionth, nor can it be reached by any calculation, analogy, or metaphor.
Śāriputra! Because these bodhisattvas and others are thus able to fulfill [the practice of] sympathetic joy, they are able to swiftly accomplish anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Śāriputra! If there are good men or good women who abide in the Mahāyāna and are further able to rejoice in this manner, they shall obtain such an immeasurable and boundless mass of great merit.
Śāriputra! If there are women who loathe their female bodies and desire to obtain male bodies, and who wish to achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they too should likewise rejoice and rejoice.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"I only pray that the World-Honored One will extensively explain for me the mass of merit obtained through exhorting [the Sangha] to reunite, so as to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all devas and humans, and also to enable the bodhisattvas of the present and future ages to gather vast roots of goodness."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Śāriputra!"
You now wish to bring benefit and happiness to many gods and humans by being able to ask the Tathāgata about such a matter.
Śāriputra, listen attentively now and reflect upon it well; I shall speak for you.
Śāriputra said: “Excellent, World-Honored One!
I now wish to hear it; I pray that you will explain it for me.”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"If there are sons or daughters of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna, they should rise from their seats at each of the three periods of the day and night, baring their right shoulders, placing their right knees on the ground, and with palms joined, speak these words:
'May the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, keep me in mind.'"

To all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, throughout all worlds in the ten directions, who have realized awakening and now desire to turn the wheel of Dharma—I now exhort all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and pray that they all turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, out of compassion for and for the sake of the peace, happiness, and benefit of all devas and humans.

Thus he spoke three times, and it was likewise repeated. "I now entreat all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones: I pray that you will turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma; I pray that those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, will bestow the gift of Dharma; I pray that the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, will universally establish Dharma assemblies; I pray that the World-Honored Ones will pour down the great rain of Dharma; I pray that the World-Honored Ones will kindle the great torch of Dharma; I pray that the World-Honored Ones will beat the great drum of Dharma; I pray that the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, will produce the music of Dharma; I pray that the World-Honored Ones will blow the great conch of Dharma; I pray that the World-Honored Ones will raise the banner of Dharma; and I pray that the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, will satisfy all sentient beings with the Dharma, enabling them to delight in the Dharma at their own will, bringing great benefit and peace to the world out of compassion for all devas and humans."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If good men or good women who wish to achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* should, during the three periods of the day and the three periods of the night, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees upon the ground, join their palms with ten fingers together, and form this thought:

'All Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, throughout all worlds in the ten directions—whether currently dwelling in the world, or abiding, or moving about—I should remember them; I should pay homage to them.'"
One should speak thus:

"To all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions who wish to relinquish their life-span and enter *nirvāṇa*, I entreat all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, not to enter *nirvāṇa* but to remain long in the world—for inconceivable eons, unspeakable, immeasurable, and incalculable eons—for the sake of bringing great benefit and peace and happiness to the gods and humans of the world; may they endure for a long time, without allowing body or mind to become weary."

Thus, having made this request three times that the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, remain long in the world for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all the devas and humans throughout immeasurable kalpas, [the Bodhisattvas] beseech them to endure remaining for a long time without allowing their body or mind to become weary.
The roots of goodness from such exhortations and requests should be dedicated toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Śāriputra, you should now consider: how much merit is obtained through such exhortation and dedication?
Śāriputra, what do you think?
If this trichiliocosm were filled with the seven treasures and one were to offer them as a gift to all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas, would the merit obtained thereby not be great?
Śāriputra said, “Very many,
World-Honored One!”
"It cannot be known through the power of thought or deliberation.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Set aside for a moment the case of the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system filled with the seven treasures."

If one were to fill the worlds of the east, south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir with the seven treasures and offer them as alms to all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas, would the merit obtained thereby not be great?
Śāriputra said: “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"It cannot be reached by the limits of conceptual thought. Śāriputra,

you should now observe that if good sons and good daughters possess right faith and are free from deceit, they can give rise to the mind of unsurpassed bodhi and can thus exhort all Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma."

Śāriputra! This accumulation of merit, compared to the previous accumulation of merit, does not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth, nor one hundred-thousandth part; it is beyond reach even by calculation or analogy.

Śāriputra! If good men and good women who have resolved their minds on awakening are able to perform such exhortations and dedications, and are able to bring their roots of goodness to fulfillment through this harmony, they shall swiftly achieve unsurpassed bodhi.
Śāriputra! When I was practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, I also constantly made such requests to the Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma and to remain long in the world.

Because I have thus exhorted the Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma, by the power of the causal conditions of those roots of goodness, Śakra, the Heavenly King, the various Brahma Kings, and others now respectfully join their palms and entreat me to turn the wheel of Dharma, saying: "We only pray that the World-Honored One will [turn the wheel of Dharma]!"
"Out of great compassion and for the sake of bringing peace, happiness, and benefit to all the worlds of devas and humans,

I turn the wheel of Dharma. Śāriputra, because in the past, when I was practicing the bodhisattva path, I exhorted the Buddhas to remain long in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma, I have now attained the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness and great compassion, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
"After my parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain for five hundred years, and the Semblance Dharma shall likewise remain for five hundred years.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Great Virtuous World-Honored One!"
How do these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna dedicate their roots of goodness toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra,

those sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna should rise from their seats during the three periods of the day and the three periods of the night, baring their right shoulders, placing their right knees upon the ground, and with palms joined, they should speak these words:”
"From the beginningless flow of birth and death until this very day, whatever accumulation of merit I have performed myself, caused others to perform, or rejoiced in seeing others perform."

Whatever merits one has cultivated toward the Three Jewels or toward individuals—whether through the practice of giving, the observance of ethical discipline, or other such meritorious deeds; whether through the performance of various meritorious acts, or even the mere thought of performing such meritorious acts; and including all acts from this point forward such as repentance, sympathetic joy, and entreaty—all these combined together are dedicated and bestowed upon all sentient beings.

Just as the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, when they formerly practiced the bodhisattva path, dedicated all their roots of goodness toward omniscience, so too do I now dedicate them; I dedicate all these roots of goodness toward unsurpassed enlightenment.

Just as all future Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, when they were practicing the bodhisattva path, dedicated their roots of goodness toward omniscience, so too do I now dedicate them; by these roots of goodness, I dedicate them all toward unsurpassed enlightenment.

All the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions, who now dwell in the world and exercise sovereign mastery—just as they, in the past when practicing the bodhisattva path, dedicated all their roots of goodness toward unsurpassed enlightenment, so too do I now likewise dedicate all my roots of goodness toward unsurpassed enlightenment.

Just as that Blessed One, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, sat at the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, abiding in the Buddha-samādhi through such inconceivable, immeasurable, vast, and stainless seals of wisdom; and having, through the wisdom of a single moment of unified correspondence, subdued the power of Māra Pāpīyas’s army and repelled them, he fully awakened to all that is to be known and seen at the time when the clear signs of dawn appeared after the night.

Having attained perfect enlightenment, he turned the unsurpassed Wheel of Dharma of the Four Noble Truths at the Deer Park in Vārāṇasī—a wheel that no ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world could ever turn.

They kindle the torch of Dharma, beat the drum of Dharma, blow the conch of Dharma, raise the banner of Dharma, and rain down the rain of Dharma; they saturate all sentient beings with the Dharma, out of great compassion for the sake of the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
They were also like those Tathāgatas: Akṣobhya, Amitābha, Siṃha, Śataprabha, Arciṣmat, Jvalanaprabha, Anantaprabha,
Kṛtapuṇyaprabha, Dīparāja, Uttama, Padmottara, Vikasita, and Ratnacandra.
Buddha, Ratnārcis Buddha, Anāvaraṇaprabhāsa Buddha, Merudhvaja Buddha, Ratnalakṣaṇa Buddha,
Mahārciskandha Buddha, Ratnadhvaja Buddha, Indradhvaja Buddha, Ratnākṣa Buddha, Candanagandha Buddha,
Niścitārci-padma-kumuda-jvalita-kāya Buddha, and Amitanāman Buddha.
He is named Glorious Light of Merit; like that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Maitreya,
and likewise all such Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who, having realized unsurpassed Buddha-enlightenment,
turn the unsurpassed, most supreme wheel of Dharma.

I am likewise; I vow to turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, and I vow to satisfy and freely bestow the gift of Dharma upon all sentient beings, for the sake of bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to the world of gods and humans, and to act for their welfare.

"Śāriputra! If there are those who hear this aforementioned supreme path, and having heard it, believe and accept it, practicing in accordance with its teachings, they shall obtain an immeasurable mass of merit."

Śāriputra! If good sons and good daughters hear this fundamental dharma of the three clusters, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, understand its meaning, and explain it extensively for others, they shall obtain a great mass of merit that is inconceivable and immeasurable.
Śāriputra! You should now contemplate such an immeasurable accumulation of merit from supernormal powers. Śāriputra!
What do you think?
Suppose all sentient beings included within this trichiliocosm were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were each to become a pratyekabuddha.

If good sons or good daughters were to provide all manner of offerings—food, drink, clothing, bedding, and medicinal requisites—for their entire lives; and after they have entered *nirvāṇa*, were to erect *śarīra* stupas ten *yojanas* in height and seven *yojanas* in length and breadth, perfectly symmetrical, adorned with exquisite colors, upright and pleasing to behold, composed of various jewels such as gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, pearl, agate, and amber; and furthermore, were to make offerings to those stupas and shrines with celestial music, scattering exquisite flower garlands, burning incense, applying fragrant unguents, and presenting silk banners, flags, and canopies as offerings.
"Would the merit obtained by that person be great?
Śāriputra replied, "It would be very great."
“World-Honored One!
It is beyond the reach of the inconceivable.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Setting aside for a moment all sentient beings encompassed within the trichiliocosm;

furthermore, let all sentient beings encompassed within as many worlds in the eastern direction as there are sands in the Ganges River, and likewise all sentient beings encompassed within such worlds in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—let them all attain human form, and having attained human form, may they realize the state of a Pratyekabuddha."

If good sons or good daughters, for as long as their lives last, provide offerings and service, supplying all manner of necessities such as clothing, food and drink, medicinal decoctions, and bedding.
"Would the merit obtained by that person not be very great?
Śāriputra replied, "It would be exceedingly great."
“World-Honored One!
It is beyond the reach of thought or calculation.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"If good sons and good daughters, being able to possess right faith and being free from deceit and crookedness, give rise to the mind of unsurpassed bodhi, and further, are able to rely upon this to perform dedication after dedication."

Śāriputra! The previous merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this mass of merit; it does not approach a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, nor can it be reached by any calculation, analogy, or metaphor.

At that time, ten thousand people from within the assembly rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, knelt with their right knees on the ground, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Great Virtuous World-Honored One!
We, too, desire to attain the unsurpassed bodhi of all Buddhas.
Why is this? O Virtuous World-Honored One!
Having heard such sūtras as these, we have conceived a profound love and joy for them.
O Great Virtuous World-Honored One!
Our aspiration and delight are set upon unsurpassed bodhi.

At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, surrounded by a retinue of sixty-eight thousand celestial beings, immediately made offerings to the Buddha and to this *Dharmaparyāya* on the Three Aggregates which had been taught, scattering upon them celestial māndārava flowers, sandalwood powder, Jambū-river gold dust, and *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers.
Having scattered [the flowers] a second and third time, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How rare, World-Honored One!

This Dharma-fundamental of the three clusters is of such great benefit that it shall purify all karmic obstructions for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and cause them to encounter and fully accomplish all wholesome dharmas."
The Buddha told Śakra: “So it is, so it is, Kauśika!”

I now proclaim this Dharma-fundamental of the three clusters for the great benefit of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others, so that they may achieve unobstructed purity regarding all phenomena and shall encounter and fully accomplish all wholesome dharmas.

Kauśika! I recall that in the past, incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago—indeed, beyond such numbers and inconceivable—there appeared in the world a Buddha named Mahārciskandha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.

Kauśika! The lifespan of that Tathāgata Mahājvālaskandha was sixty-eight thousand billion years; his first assembly consisted of one hundred thousand śrāvakas, his second assembly consisted of nine billion nine hundred million śrāvakas, and his third assembly consisted of nine billion eight hundred million śrāvakas.
Kauśika! That Tathāgata Mahārciskandha brings great benefit to the devas and humans.
At that time, there was a woman in that assembly named Satmātṛkā who was seated among them.

Having heard this Dharma-fundamental of the three aggregates from that Tathāgata Great Mass of Flames, they accepted it with faith, recited it, explained it extensively for others, practiced according to the teaching, and gave rise to the mind of unsurpassed bodhi.

Upon hearing this Dharma, she immediately transformed her female body into a male body; she will constantly be born among gods and humans as they cycle through saṃsāra, and shall receive eighty-four thousand bodies of universal monarchs (cakravartin).

He currently resides there in the eastern direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of buddha-fields from this buddha-field, having manifested the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and is known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnajvālāskandha.
Kauśika! If there are sentient beings who, at the time of their death, hear the name of that Tathāgata Ratnārcis-kūṭa and are able to keep it in mind, they shall never again receive a female body.
Why is this? When that Tathāgata Ratnārcis-ghana was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this vow:
"If there be any woman who, at the time of her death, hears my name and is able to keep it in mind, she shall never again receive a female body."

"Kauśika! This Dharma-fundamental of the three aggregates is capable of producing such manifold benefit; it shall cause all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to fully purify all dharmas and all obstructive karmas, and they shall encounter and achieve the full perfection of all wholesome dharmas."

When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, Śakra-devānām-indra, the Elder Śāriputra, and all the devas, nāgas, gandharvas, asuras, humans, non-humans, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Threefold Vow of Repentance (Mahāyāna-tri-saṃvara-pratikramaṇa-sūtra)
